title: Antiferromagnetic order and lattice response in DyCuAs$_2$
authors: M. G. Kim, J. -W. Kim, P. Ryan, D. Evans, E. D. Mun
abstract: We report high-resolution synchrotron X-ray diffraction and X-ray resonant magnetic scattering (XRMS) studies of the low-temperature crystal and magnetic structures of DyCuAs$_2$, a member of the \RE{}CuAs$_2$ family exhibiting a resistivity minimum above the antiferromagnetic transition temperature. Synchrotron diffraction measurements reveal that DyCuAs$_2$ preserves tetragonal symmetry down to low temperature within the experimental resolution, although pronounced anomalies in both lattice parameters $a$ and $c$ are observed near the antiferromagnetic transition temperature, $T_{\mathrm N}\approx7$~K, indicating strong magnetoelastic coupling. XRMS measurements at the Dy $L_3$ edge establish commensurate antiferromagnetic ordering below $T_{\mathrm N}$ with AFM Bragg peaks at \qq{} = (0, 0, 0.5). Representation analysis and calculations of the AFM Bragg peak intensities identify the magnetic structure as the $Γ_{10}$ representation, consisting of in-plane Dy moments stacked along the \cc{} axis in a $++--$ sequence. The magnetic structure is therefore identical to that previously reported for SmCuAs$_2$. Comparison among DyCuAs$_2$, SmCuAs$_2$, and GdCuAs$_2$ suggests that in-plane AFM order and the associated magnetic frustration on the tetragonal lattice are closely connected to the emergence of the resistivity minimum in the \RE{}CuAs$_2$ family. At the same time, the enhanced lattice response and stronger magnetic-field sensitivity observed in DyCuAs$_2$ imply that magnetoelastic and spin-orbit interactions additionally play important roles in determining the robustness of this anomalous transport behavior.
summary: This experimental study characterizes the magnetic and structural properties of DyCuAs2, revealing a commensurate in-plane antiferromagnetic order below 7 K. By comparing it to other members of the RECuAs2 family, the authors propose that magnetic frustration arising from this in-plane AFM order is the common cause for an anomalous resistivity minimum, with magnetoelastic and spin-orbit interactions playing a crucial role in its robustness.
main_problem: The study investigates the interplay between antiferromagnetic (AFM) order and lattice response in the RECuAs2 family, aiming to understand the origin of an anomalous resistivity minimum observed above the AFM transition temperature.
main_result: The magnetic structure is determined to be a commensurate AFM ordering ($\Gamma_{10}$ representation) with in-plane moments, suggesting that in-plane AFM order and associated magnetic frustration are key ingredients for the resistivity minimum.
method: The research combines high-resolution synchrotron X-ray diffraction (XRD) for structural analysis and X-ray resonant magnetic scattering (XRMS) for determining the magnetic structure.
model_or_system: The physical system is the RECuAs2 family of compounds, where the rare earth element (RE) dictates the magnetic moment and coupling strength. The analysis compares DyCuAs2 to SmCuAs2 and GdCuAs2 to isolate the role of magnetic interactions.
key_observables: Resistivity minimum ($ho(T)$), lattice parameters ($a$ and $c$), AFM Bragg peak intensity and position ($\mathbf{q}=(0, 0, 0.5)$), and magnetic susceptibility/magnetization ($M(H)$).
important_parameters: Antiferromagnetic transition temperature ($T_N \approx 7$ K), magnetic moment magnitude ($\mu_B$), and applied magnetic field strength ($H$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the preservation of tetragonal symmetry down to low temperatures, despite observing strong magnetoelastic coupling anomalies in the lattice parameters near $T_N$.
figures_summary: Figures show the temperature dependence of resistivity (with a minimum near 15 K), structural Bragg scans confirming symmetry, and temperature dependence of lattice parameters $a$ and $c$ exhibiting anomalies near $T_N$.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by characterizing the structural and magnetic transitions using XRD and XRMS, establishing the AFM structure, and then correlating the observed magnetic ordering and lattice anomalies with the anomalous transport behavior (resistivity minimum) across the RECuAs2 series.
why_interesting: The strong coupling between magnetic ordering, lattice strain (magnetoelastic coupling), and anomalous electronic transport (resistivity minimum) provides a rich platform for studying emergent quantum phenomena in strongly correlated materials.

Figure 1(a) presents the electrical resistivity of DyCuAs2. The zero-ﬁeld electrical resistivity of DyCuAs2 up to 300 K exhibits metallic behavior at high temperatures, followed by an unexpected minimum near 15 K, as shown in Fig. 1(a). Upon further cooling, ρ(T ) increases and reaches a peak at the N´eel temperature, TN (≈7 K), before decreasing rapidly below the onset of antiferromagnetic ordering. As shown in the inset of Fig. 1(a), the resistivity minimum is progressively sup- pressed with increasing magnetic ﬁeld applied parallel to the ab plane (H ∥ab) and disappears completely at H ≥30 kOe.
